D002-D005_h001.question:
It's hard to pin down when things really started going downhill, but I guess it’s been… for a good few years now. I’m 48, and my wife, she’s noticed it too. Driving the subway used to be second nature, but now, I make a lot of stupid errors, things I’d never have overlooked before. Sometimes I miss a station stop or forget to make an announcement. It sounds simple, but it throws the whole schedule off.

It’s not just work. At home, I try to help out, but then I'll forget what I was doing halfway through a chore. She’ll ask me to fix something, and I just don’t follow through. What’s really weird, though, is how my mind gets… hijacked. I’ll be trying to focus on something important, and then a voice, not a real one, will tell me to stop, or that there's a pattern in the rails I need to follow that’s not actually there. Or I feel others are distracting me with their thoughts. This all started happening before these strange voices and thoughts really took hold, but it definitely got worse *after* they did. My mind just races, or I feel this buzzing sort of restlessness that makes it hard to sit still, especially when the voices are louder. It’s like trying to listen to the dispatch over constant static in my head.
D002-D005_h001.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

It really started getting bad about eight months ago, when I began hearing whispers when no one was around, and seeing things out of the corner of my eye.
